criteria_outcomes.criterion: Map capabilities to needs without changing the stipulated need text.

reviews.decision_reason: map_coverage retained the handoff rows, preserved record_id and need as received, and produced direct coverage only when a capability need exactly matched; all coverage is none because the upstream handoff need values are source IDs rather than stipulated need text.

criteria_outcomes.criterion: Order unsupported needs first and otherwise preserve upstream ranking.

reviews.decision_reason: prioritize consumed coverage and evidence_sources, assigned unsupported status from coverage, carried upstream_rank from provenance, and ordered rows by unsupported status then upstream rank.

criteria_outcomes.criterion: Produce the deterministic top-need recommendation and decision required by the execution contract.

reviews.decision_reason: synthesize retained eight ranked priorities and built the recommendation from the first priority row, yielding decision prioritize and top_need s01 as dictated by the actual ranked input.

criteria_outcomes.criterion: Select every qualifying demand row and preserve record_id, need, demand_score, source_id, and source_weight fields.
Treat the supplied corpus and capabilities as stipulated test inputs.

reviews.decision_reason: select_demand selected all qualifying corpus rows but did not preserve the stipulated need field; it wrote source_id into need, turning descriptive need text into s01 through s08. This is the root cause of the downstream all-unsupported coverage.

criteria_outcomes.criterion: Select every qualifying demand row and preserve record_id, need, demand_score, source_id, and source_weight fields.

reviews.decision_reason: normalize preserved the selected rows it received, enforced the allowed record identifiers, kept the required columns, and bounded the output to the eight-row index window. The bad need values were already present in its input.
assemble_provenance ranked all normalized rows deterministically by demand_score descending and record_id, preserving record_id, source_id, and source_weight into evidence_sources.
